name: C5: a newer generation no longer stops the running pass
why: The generation check after each yield is gone: a pass a synchronous runFilter() (here the ✕ clear) replaced runs on and commits its result over the newer one.

name: C5: a synchronous runFilter() no longer cancels a sliced pass
why: runFilter() stops taking a generation, so the ✕ clear's own pass leaves the sliced one current and it redraws the filtered rows afterwards.

name: C5: a replaced pass stores its partial result
why: On going stale the pass caches what it matched so far under its key.

name: C5: a replaced pass writes the narrowing state
why: On going stale the pass leaves its half-done match set as _incrMatchSet, so the next key would narrow from it.

name: C5: _renderSettled is not held while the pass compares
why: The pass no longer publishes its pending promise, so the header-count scan and the card see a settled table mid-pass.

name: C5: a stale chunked render keeps drawing
why: KNOWN GAP, recorded honestly: the pass no longer bumps _renderGeneration, so a chunked render of the previous result would go on drawing. No fixture is over 500 rows, so renderRowsChunked never has a second chunk to abort in any spec; the perf A/B on artist-events is what exercises it.

name: C5: no row-array identity check
why: KNOWN OVERLAP, recorded honestly: without the identity check a sort is still caught, because the sort's own runFilter() takes a generation. The check is for a fetch or disk load that replaces the arrays without filtering at once, which no spec drives mid-pass.

name: C5: sliced and synchronous results differ
why: The single-table job is handed a context without the global query, so it matches every row and caches that under the real key: the same number of slices, the wrong answer.

name: C5 mobile: sliced and synchronous results differ
why: Each multi-table job is handed a context without the global query: the same slices, every row matches; seen through the touch path.

name: C6a: initCollapsableColumns measures column by column again
why: Each column is measured and finished before the next is measured, so every column's writes force the next column's reads to lay out the table again.
grep: reads all columns in at most two groups

name: C6b: applyStickyColumn reads inside the write pass again
why: A getComputedStyle per row in pass 1, between that row's writes and the next row's: one style recalculation per row.

name: C6b: the row hover is no longer wired
why: The restructured pass 3 forgets the mouseenter listener: hovering a row no longer paints it.

name: C6e: the prebuilt clones are never handed over
why: The commit clones synchronously again: the slices did the work for nothing and the long block is back.
grep: single-table: a sliced pass shows exactly

name: C6e: a changed cell expand state does not discard the clones
why: Clones built before a cell-toggle click are drawn anyway, with that cell's old expand state.

name: C6e: the clone phase does not notice it was replaced
why: No staleness check after a clone slice: a pass replaced while cloning commits its old result.

name: C6e: the multi-table commit ignores the prebuilt clones
why: runFilter's multi branch stops looking up the hand-over; only the single-table path would use it.
grep: multi-table: a sliced pass shows exactly

name: C6e: a key in the global filter no longer makes the running pass outdated

name: C6g: an outdated pass throws its complete result away
why: Outdated by a key, the pass finishes comparing but stores nothing, so the next pass compares the whole table again.

name: C6g: the next pass does not wait for an outdated one
why: It takes a generation at once, so the outdated pass becomes stale, stores nothing, and the new pass compares everything.

name: C6g: an outdated pass stores after a cache invalidation
why: The epoch is not checked: a result computed before an invalidation is put back into the cache.
